task.description:
HARD GATE (WF-01 Step 2) on REQ-ANALYST's seven new requirements, REQ-225 through REQ-231, drafted into docs/requirements.yaml for ISS-0438 (the entity/data-model subsystem port). Read docs/requirements.yaml in full for context (existing schema, and read all seven new entries plus their neighbors). For EACH of the seven, independently check: (a) TESTABILITY -- vague words ('appropriately', 'as needed', 'reasonably') fail; (b) CONSISTENCY -- no conflict with any done requirement (specifically REQ-202, REQ-203, REQ-024, all cited as dependencies) or any docs/migration/decisions/ record; (c) DEPENDS_ON CORRECTNESS -- not just non-orphaned, genuinely required before that slice can start, in the right order; (d) STAGE FIT -- S6 is the correct stage per the design artefact's own reasoning (read lib/letflow/design/iss0438-entity-subsystem-scoping.md section 1's 'Target stage' subsection for the argument -- verify it, don't just trust it); (e) SIZE -- one agent turn each, not multiple unrelated deliverables bundled. Also verify REQ-230 (the query-DSL compiler slice) correctly reads as touching a tenant-data path (SQL compilation over tenant-scoped entity records) so it will correctly route through SECURITY-REVIEWER at WF-02 implementation time -- if its description doesn't make that scope clear, that is a real gap to FAIL on, not a nice-to-have.

Also independently verify the three open design questions the handoff instructions required REQ-ANALYST to name explicitly (JsonSchema cross-namespace reuse in REQ-227, entity ownership model in REQ-225, synthetic-instance-per-type in REQ-228) are actually present in those requirements' text, not silently resolved and not omitted -- spot check by reading each cited requirement's actual description text yourself.

Also verify docs/migration/stage-6-operational-cross-cutting.md's addendum paragraph was actually added (read the file's tail) and that it appends rather than rewrites the existing 'S6 is now complete' line.

If ANY check fails: FAIL, listing issues by requirement id and check letter, per WF-01 Step 2's own acceptance criteria. If all pass: PASS.
acceptance_criteria: Every check (a-e) actually run against each of the seven new requirements individually, not assumed or impressionistic
Any FAIL cites the specific requirement id and which check failed
The tenant-data-path scope of REQ-230 (SQL compiler) is explicitly confirmed or flagged as missing
The three named open design questions' presence in their respective requirement descriptions is independently spot-checked, not trusted from REQ-ANALYST's own report
The stage-6-operational-cross-cutting.md addendum is confirmed present and additive (not a rewrite)
